title: Bittensor Daily News — November 3, 2026
summary: TAO joins Virtune’s AI index basket. Lium and Cascade merge rental fixes, while REAX documents a smaller inference budget.

ecosystem.headline: TAO joins Virtune’s new AI crypto index basket
ecosystem.summary: Virtune’s November 3 issuer announcement includes TAO among 13 equally weighted assets in its physically backed AI Crypto Index ETP. Its stated first trading day is November 3 on Nasdaq Stockholm (VIRAI) and Xetra (VRTI). Quarterly rebalancing and a 1.49% annual management fee apply. This basket is separate from Virtune’s existing single-asset Bittensor ETP. No fund inflows, TAO purchase quantity or price impact were established.
ecosystem.ratingReason: A concrete documented development, with commercial significance and independent execution limited as described.

updates.headline: SN8 Vanta records a finalized burn of 118.847474634 alpha
updates.summary: A successful AlphaBurned event at finalized block 9,427,005, extrinsic 12, destroyed exactly 118.847474634 Vanta alpha on November 3 at 17:42:12 UTC. Historical before/after identity and registration 1,477,264 identify SN8 Vanta. The transaction crosses the 100-alpha individual-event threshold and is retained in the Burns archive. It is a direct alpha burn; no TAO purchase, customer revenue or buyback funding was established. Fees and smaller events are excluded from this public amount.

updates.headline: SN51 Lium merges a check for slow GPU upload links
updates.summary: Lium merged PR1950 on November 3 to add a 10 Mbps upload-speed moving-average floor to VerifyX alongside the download check. A weak uplink can hinder data-heavy rentals even when download speed passes. Missing, NaN, zero and first-unmeasured observations have documented exceptions. The code merge is verified; production rollout was not independently tested.
updates.ratingReason: A concrete documented development, with commercial significance and independent execution limited as described.

updates.headline: SN70 Fugal opens cost-aware model routing competition and joins Yuma
updates.summary: On November 3, Fugal announced miner registration and scoring for its SN70 routing competition; Yuma separately confirmed Accelerator participation. The router aims to choose a model according to both predicted answer quality and cost. Its public repository documents Intel TDX-attested evaluation and published epoch results, giving miners a concrete route to compete on routing efficiency. These are team launch claims and published implementation details: this review did not independently run the router, verify completed scoring epochs or establish customer savings. The announcement does not establish a new subnet registration or a completed ownership transfer.

sources.label: Fugal launch announcement, November 3 at 12:14 PM Eastern
Official router subnet implementation and scoring documentation

updates.ratingReason: Actionable launch documentation and confirmed accelerator participation; completed live scoring and commercial adoption were not independently established.

updates.headline: SN91 Cascade separates replacement GPU rental clocks
updates.summary: Cascade merged PR421 on November 3 to track spend by individual rent ID rather than a reused pod name. The described failure let a short replacement rental inherit the previous machine’s start time, inflating make-good accounting and triggering a spend cap. The trainer-side fix separates rent records and keeps make-good owed out of the waste-cap pause decision. Merged code does not establish that every running trainer has upgraded.
updates.ratingReason: A concrete documented development, with commercial significance and independent execution limited as described.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX documents a smaller inference reward budget
updates.summary: REAX’s November 2 mining documentation assigns inference 30% of its miner reward budget from the first weight set at or after November 2 at 14:30 UTC, down from 40%. REAX Engine 20% and generalist 30% remain listed; both competitions are paused without a next crowning. Unpaid portions follow the published burn rule. Actual validator application was not reconstructed. These within-miner allocations are separate from the chain’s five-slot eTAO vector.

sources.label: Official mining policy and dated status

updates.ratingReason: A concrete documented development, with commercial significance and independent execution limited as described.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX releases a two-part decision model with open weights and an EU API listing
updates.summary: REAX announced version 1.3 on November 3 at 12:05 PM Eastern. The public model card identifies contributions from SN92 miners UID18 and UID83, blended with existing open models; its two parts run in parallel and combine option probabilities. Published weights, attribution and MIT engine code provide a reproducible release path. Decision Models lists reax-1.3 in its EU API at EUR0.40 or USD0.40 per million input tokens, with output free. This turns competition output into a published decision-model product. The release graphic reports the team’s own measurements, not official leaderboard scores; official submission was still pending in its announcement. This review did not execute paid inference or independently reproduce performance.

sources.label: REAX 1.3 release and qualification thread, November 3

Official EU API model listing and price

updates.ratingReason: Concrete public model artifacts and a hosted product listing extend beyond competition mechanics, but comparative results remain internal and independent usage or performance was not established.
